input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# KServe serving-stack image FIPS 140-3 conversion

## Description

Converts the KServe component's serving-stack images so they run correctly on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no
non-validated crypto in the request path. This epic also produces the crypto
module inventory, build attestations, and test results for the KServe images
(inputs to the compliance evidence package) and wires a gating CI check that
prevents FIPS regressions in KServe builds.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe serving-stack images for linked cryptographic libraries;
  classify each as validated or non-validated and record the result as a
  per-image module inventory (the strategy does not enumerate the affected
  images — this audit produces the definitive list).
- Replace or rebuild non-validated crypto usage so the images run on
  FIPS-enabled clusters using validated modules; the request path must contain
  no non-validated crypto.
- Verify correct runtime behavior of the converted images on FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift clusters (inference request serving, InferenceService status
  handling).
- Add a gating CI check to the KServe build pipeline that fails any
  serving-stack build reintroducing non-validated crypto usage, and verify the
  check passes on the converted images and fails on a deliberately
  non-compliant build.
- Keep the KServe build pipeline green after the conversion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every KServe serving-stack image in scope runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster and uses validated cryptographic modules, with no
  non-validated crypto in the request path.
- A module inventory exists for every KServe image in scope, classifying each
  linked crypto library as validated or non-validated, in a form suitable for
  inclusion in the compliance evidence package.
- Build attestations and FIPS test results for the converted KServe images
  are produced and available to the compliance evidence package.
- A gating CI check fails any KServe serving-stack build that reintroduces
  non-validated crypto usage, and passes on the converted images.
- The KServe build pipeline is green for the converted images.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the KServe share of "all serving-stack images run correctly on
  FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto
  in the request path)".
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the FIPS regression gating check for KServe builds is
  delivered here rather than as a separate epic — it enforces the same build
  surfaces this epic converts, so it is not independently deferrable and
  splitting it would require a second wiring pass over the same pipelines.
- HLR-2 (P0, slice): module inventory, build attestations, and test results
  for the KServe images, aggregated into the compliance evidence package by
  the evidence/submission work.

## Risks / Notes

- Specific remediation choices (which validated modules replace which
  libraries, per-language crypto provider configuration) are implementation
  decisions for the team; the strategy deliberately leaves them open.
- If the image audit materially exceeds the strategy's "several images"
  estimate, re-scope before continuing.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and submission

## Description

Assembles the serving-stack FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package — module
inventory, build attestations, and test results produced by the KServe and
Platform Operator conversion work — and drives it through the mandatory
security review board submission to the external accredited certification lab.

## Scope

- Aggregate the per-image module inventories, build attestations, and FIPS
  test results produced by the serving-stack conversion work for all images in
  scope.
- Assemble the evidence package in the form required by the security review
  board and the external certification lab.
- Submit the package through the security review board, triage findings, and
  resolve them until the package is accepted for progression.
- Prepare and deliver the submission package to the external accredited
  certification lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, build
  attestations, and test results covering every serving-stack image in scope,
  with no gaps against the inventories produced by the conversion work.
- The evidence package is submitted to the security review board and triaged
  to acceptance for progression to the external certification lab.
- The submission package is delivered to the external accredited certification
  lab.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): "A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab."
- Consumes the HLR-1 deliverables (converted images and their per-image
  evidence inputs) from the conversion work.

## Risks / Notes

- The accredited lab's historical turnaround is six to nine months, and the
  security review board meets on its own cadence; both are externally
  controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. They dominate the
  schedule and belong in delivery planning, not in this epic's acceptance
  criteria.
- The certification grant itself is the lab's decision; this epic's completion
  point is the assembled, review-board-triaged, lab-delivered package.

# FIPS support posture documentation for the model serving stack

## Description

Documents the FIPS 140-3 support posture of the model serving stack and the
cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters,
reflecting the implemented state of the conversion and compliance work.

## Scope

Content outline:

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: what is supported — serving
  stack images running on FIPS-enabled clusters with validated cryptographic
  modules — and the relationship between that posture and the external
  certification status.
- Cluster prerequisites: what a cluster must provide (FIPS-enabled OpenShift,
  any required configuration) to run the serving stack in its FIPS posture.
- Boundaries: explicitly out-of-scope areas (FIPS posture for workbenches,
  pipelines, and training; Common Criteria certification) so support statements are unambiguous.
- Supporting detail drawn from the compliance evidence (module inventory
  highlights, what the regression check guarantees), kept consistent with the
  assembled evidence package.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture for the model
  serving stack.
- Published documentation states the cluster prerequisites for running the
  model serving stack on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  conversion and the compliance evidence package for accuracy — no statement
  contradicts the module inventory, test results, or certification status.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): "Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites."

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

Triage: neither below-threshold nor docs-only. The strategy is Critical-priority
compliance work spanning multiple architecturally distinct work streams (image
conversion in two components, a compliance/security process with human gates,
and substantive documentation), so it proceeds through full decomposition.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | KServe serving-stack image FIPS 140-3 conversion | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | Platform Operator FIPS 140-3 conversion | Implementation | RHOAI Platform (assumed — see Health Warnings) | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | FIPS support posture documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Serving (assumed — see Health Warnings) | P0 |

Note on E004's priority: per the docs-authoring priority exception, docs epics
derive priority from the strategy frontmatter (`priority: Critical` → P0), not
from HLR-4's P2 label, and do not push priority upstream.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe FIPS conversion"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator FIPS conversion"]
    E003["E003 Compliance evidence package"]
    E004["E004 FIPS documentation"]
    E001 --> E003
    E002 --> E003
    E001 --> E004
    E002 --> E004
    E003 --> E004
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumption) | The evidence package aggregates the module inventory, build attestations, and test results the KServe conversion produces; it cannot be assembled before those artifacts exist. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumption) | Same — the evidence package consumes the Platform Operator conversion's inventory, attestations, and test results. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation must describe the implemented FIPS posture; blocked by every Implementation epic. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Same — the evidence epic is an Implementation epic, and the documentation's support statements must reflect the assembled compliance posture, not contradict it. |

Non-edges (parallel / merged work):

- **E001 ∥ E002** — different components in different repos with no shared
  artifacts (Rule 14); both conversions run in parallel.
- **HLR-3 (CI FIPS regression check) is not a standalone epic.** It is a
  shared-surface enforcement deliverable over the same build surfaces being
  converted. Per the per-surface division rule, each conversion epic delivers
  and verifies the gating check for its own component's builds; a standalone
  CI epic would carve one logical change into a work-type epic and leave each
  conversion epic's slice incomplete.
- **HLR-2's module inventory is likewise divided per surface**: each
  conversion epic produces the crypto module inventory for its own images, and
  the evidence epic aggregates. No standalone inventory epic.
- **No Investigation epics.** The strategy's Open Questions section states
  "None on scope"; no risks table, assumptions, conditional ADRs, or pending
  reviews exist. The externally controlled lab/review-board timing affects the
  schedule, not which epics exist or what they do, so it is a risk note on the
  evidence epic, not an unknown requiring resolution work.
- **No konflux-onboarding / repo-onboarding / license-validation epics.** KServe
  is already Konflux-onboarded (architecture context). Platform Operator is an
  existing canonical component whose images the strategy treats as existing;
  see Health Warnings for the missing-context caveat.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001 (KServe images), E002 (Platform Operator images) | Split by component boundary (Rule 1); each epic covers its component's serving-stack images. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 (aggregation + submission), with inventory/attestation/test-result slices in E001 and E002 | E003 assembles and submits the package; the per-image inputs are produced by the conversion epics (per-surface division). |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001, E002 (bundled) | Bundled: the CI gating check enforces the very build surfaces the P0 conversion work converts — it shares the build/pipeline surface with the P0 work and is not independently deferrable; splitting it would produce a standalone work-type epic plus a second wiring pass over the same pipelines. Per the shared-surface rule, the check's slice is delivered and verified inside each conversion epic. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 | Standalone docs-authoring epic (substantive new doc content, per the work-product-type boundary). Priority P0 via the docs-authoring exception (strategy priority Critical → P0). |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then), no
   Non-Functional Requirements, and no Technical Approach / Staff Engineer
   Input. The decomposition proceeded from the HLRs and Affected Components;
   per-epic acceptance criteria were derived from HLR text and the
   implementation rules.
2. **Team assignments are assumptions.** KServe's owner (RHOAI Serving) comes
   from the architecture context (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`). The
   Platform Operator owner (RHOAI Platform) and the documentation owner (RHOAI
   Serving) are not stated anywhere in the strategy — confirm before
   scheduling.
3. **Scope ambiguity — "serving data plane".** The problem statement says
   "KServe components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto
   libraries", but Affected Components lists only KServe and Platform
   Operator. If "serving data plane" is intended to include Serving Runtimes
   images (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit are KServe's model-execution dependencies
   per architecture context), an additional conversion epic for Serving
   Runtimes is needed and the evidence epic's scope widens. The strategy
   asserts no open scope questions, so this is flagged for human verification
   rather than spun into an Investigation epic. Relatedly, "several images" is
   never enumerated — the per-image audit is a deliverable of each conversion
   epic.
4. **Platform Operator has no architecture-context file.** Its maturity,
   owning team, and Konflux onboarding status cannot be corroborated. It is an
   existing canonical RHAI component (present in `.context/rhai-components.txt`)
   and the strategy treats its images as already existing, so no onboarding
   chain was generated; this missing context is why E002's
   `architecture_claims` signal is 0. If the Platform Operator build pipeline
   is not Konflux-onboarded, a `konflux-onboarding` epic may need adding —
   kept parallel with E002 per Rule 10, never as a dependency edge.
5. **Externally controlled schedule, deliberately not ACs.** The accredited
   lab's six-to-nine-month historical turnaround and the security review
   board's cadence dominate the schedule and cannot be compressed by
   engineering effort. They are recorded as risks on the evidence epic; that
   epic's acceptance criteria stop at the engineering completion point the
   strategy controls (package assembled, submitted through the review board,
   triaged, delivered to the lab) — the certification decision itself is the
   lab's, not an AC.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable as a DAG split. The external party with uncertain timing (the
accredited certification lab) gates no engineering epic: all conversion, CI,
and evidence-assembly work proceeds regardless, and Tier-1 value (HLR-1/HLR-3 —
images running correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters with regression enforcement)
is delivered by E001/E002 independent of the certification outcome. Only the
certification decision itself waits on the lab, and that is outside
engineering control.
